definition_short: A pawn reaching the far rank is replaced, as part of the same move, by a queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour.
definition_long:
A pawn reaching the eighth rank (first rank for Black) must be exchanged, as part of the same move, for a new queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour. The choice is not restricted to pieces already captured, and there is no limit on how many of a kind may be on the board.

FIDE Art. 4.6 governs the physical act: 'the pawn does not have to be placed on the square of arrival', the order of removing pawn and placing piece does not matter, and 'if an opponent's piece stands on the square of promotion, it must be captured.' Art. 4.4.4: the choice is finalised when the new piece touches the promotion square.

Choosing something other than a queen is UNDERPROMOTION, and is correct when a queen would stalemate, or when a knight's move is what the position needs (a check or fork a queen cannot give).
epistemic_note: Official rule. Underpromotion is a consequence of the rule, not a separate rule.

preconditions: A pawn is moving to the eighth rank (White) or first rank (Black)

exceptions: Promotion is compulsory: a pawn may not remain a pawn.
Underpromotion to a rook avoids stalemate where a queen would cause it; underpromotion to a knight gains a check or fork unavailable to a queen.

explanation_templates.beginner: A pawn reaching the far end of the board turns into another piece — almost always a queen.
explanation_templates.intermediate: Promotion. A queen is right nearly always, but check for stalemate, and check whether a knight would give a decisive check or fork.
explanation_templates.advanced: Art. 3.7.5 / 4.6. Underpromotion is justified by stalemate avoidance or by knight geometry.
